response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.ordertune AS t, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS n FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark GROUP BY o.ordertune), s AS (SELECT t, n, n * 1.0 / SUM(n) OVER () AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT t, n, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(n) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_overall FROM a WHERE share > avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: Orders are identified by orders.orderspivot (the primary key) for distinct counting; each order has one order type, so the shares sum to 1 and the overall average share equals 1 divided by the number of groups (including the NULL group).
The inner join to orders removes executions with no matching order. Only orders that have at least one execution are counted.
